To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inhibition of the activities of ATP-CL and FAS by long chain fatty acids and their coenzyme A esters was reversed by purified fatty acid binding protein and the activity of these enzymes increased with the advancement in gestation.

the fatty acid synthase (FAS) and ATP citrate lyase (ACL) are the two important key enzymes in fatty acid metabolism in developing human brain and the fatty acid binding protein (FABP) plays an important role in the regulation of these enzymes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of lipid synthesis in developing human brain.
the role of fatty acid binding proteins in the modulation of fatty acid metabolism in the developing human brain.
the regulation of the synthesis of long-chain fatty acids in developing human brain by fatty acid binding protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fatty acids are the most potent inhibitors of ATP-citrate-lyase and fatty acid synthesis.
fatty acid binding protein is involved in the regulation of fatty acid synthesis and its precursors by binding to fatty acids and their derivatives.
the fatty acid binding protein is an important regulator of fatty acid synthetase activity in the developing brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fatty acid binding protein is a key regulator of the fatty acid metabolism in human fetal brain.

fatty acid binding protein (FABP), a protein that has been found in the brain, reverses the inhibition of ATP-citrate-lyase and fatty acid-syntase by fatty acids and fatty acid-CoA esters and activates the enzymes when added alone.
the fatty acids and their esters are the inhibitors of ATP-CL and FA synthase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fatty acid binding protein is a key player in the regulation of fatty acid synthesis.
the inhibition of fatty acid synthesis by fatty acids in developing brain is prevented by a protein that is present in brain and is specific for fatty acid binding.
the inhibitory effect of free fatty acid on fatty acid synthetase and ATP citrate lyase is reversed by fatty acid binding protein and the protein itself activates the enzymes.
